newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sees no change in oil output, exports in 97.
newsitem.headline: Russia sees no change in oil output, exports in 97.

text.p: Russia's Fuel and Energy Ministry does not expect major changes in crude oil and oil product output and exports this year, First Deputy Fuel and Energy Minister Sergei Kiriyenko said on Tuesday.
"We do not expect any big changes this year," he told a news briefing, when asked about his forecast for output and exports this year.

Russia, the world's third largest oil producer, produced 293 million tonnes (5.86 million barrels per day) of oil in 1996, according to State Statistics Committee figures. This was two percent down on year-ago levels and roughly half Russia's peak oil output during the late 1980s.
It exported 105 million tonnes (2.1 million bpd) to non-Commonwealth of Independent States countries (CIS), up nine percent from 1995.
Russia refined 176 million tonnes of oil (3.52 million bpd), down three percent from 1995 levels.
Non-CIS exports of oil products rose to 54.88 million tonnes in 1996 from 43.55 million in 1995.
